Phần ví dụ còn hơi chung chung, chưa có tên một dự án hoặc nghiên cứu cụ thể để tăng tính thuyết phục.

Sân, hồ bơi, phòng tập gần, an toàn, giá phải chăng gỡ rào cản khoảng cách và chi phí; người ta tập nhiều hơn khi tiện. Ví dụ hồ bơi công mới ở khu nghèo; ít béo phì, tim, tiểu đường, tâm thần tốt hơn; trẻ yêu thể thao duy trì khi lớn; nơi gặp gỡ giảm cô đơn cho người già.

essays.question: How far do you think nanotechnology will influence medicine in the next 20 years? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Nanotechnology, which works with materials thousands of times thinner than a human hair, is attracting growing attention in medicine. I believe that it will influence medicine to a moderate but important extent over the next twenty years, mainly through better drug delivery and detection of disease, although most applications are still at an early stage.

First and foremost, nanotechnology could deliver drugs exactly where they are needed. Tiny particles can carry medicine directly to a tumour, sparing healthy tissue, and tiny sensors may detect disease much earlier than current tests. Chemotherapy, for example, damages healthy cells as well as cancer cells, so a treatment aimed only at the tumour could reduce side effects such as hair loss and weakness. Researchers are also developing coatings that help implants to resist infection and fabrics that can protect wounds. If these ideas succeed, patients will suffer less and recover faster.

However, the influence will be limited in the near future. Many nano treatments remain at the laboratory stage, and testing for safety takes a long time, because very small particles may behave unpredictably inside the body. Costs are high, so new products may reach wealthy patients first, and regulators will require clear evidence that the benefits outweigh the risks. Some effects on the environment when particles are released are also unknown. Progress is therefore likely to be gradual, with a few important treatments arriving rather than a sudden revolution.

In conclusion, nanotechnology is likely to influence medicine to a moderate extent through more targeted treatment and earlier detection, but safety testing and cost will slow its spread.

essays.question: To what extent should governments regulate fast-food outlets near schools? Give reasons for your answer.

versions.text:
Many children pass fast-food outlets on their way to and from school, and some people argue that governments should regulate them. I largely agree, since children are especially vulnerable to cheap, convenient fast food near their school, although rules should be fair to small businesses.

To begin with, children are especially vulnerable to cheap, convenient fast food near their school. Young people have little money, little self-control and habits that are still forming, so an outlet at the school gate makes unhealthy eating the default. Pupils who buy chips and fizzy drinks from a shop next to the school every lunchtime, for example, take in far more sugar and fat than they realise. Childhood obesity is rising in many countries, and it can lead to diabetes and heart problems later in life. Restricting nearby outlets reduces temptation and supports the healthy meals that schools provide.

Furthermore, only governments can set rules that apply to everyone. Parents and teachers can advise children, but they cannot control what is sold outside the gate, and a single outlet that changes its menu may lose customers to a rival. Planning rules, such as limiting new outlets within a certain distance of schools, create a level playing field and send a clear message about public health. However, regulation is not enough on its own. Pupils can still buy food elsewhere, and small businesses depend on their income, so existing outlets should be given time and support to offer healthier options. Education about nutrition and good school meals are also needed so that children make better choices even when temptation exists.

In conclusion, governments should regulate fast-food outlets near schools to a large extent, because children are vulnerable and habits form early, provided that the rules are fair and combined with education.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: chính phủ nên điều tiết quán ăn nhanh gần trường đến mức nào — largely agree

plan.think: Mở bài nêu hình ảnh (trẻ đi ngang quán ăn nhanh trên đường đi học) rồi largely agree + lý do + giới hạn (công bằng với doanh nghiệp nhỏ).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — trẻ dễ bị tác động
plan.think: Trẻ ít tiền, ít tự chủ, thói quen đang hình thành; quán ngay cổng trường biến ăn không lành mạnh thành mặc định. Ví dụ học sinh mua khoai chiên và nước ngọt mỗi giờ trưa. Béo phì trẻ em dẫn đến tiểu đường và bệnh tim.

essays.question: Some people say that international sporting events are a waste of money. Do you agree or disagree?

versions.text:
The Olympic Games, the football World Cup and other international sporting events cost host countries enormous sums, and some people say that they are a waste of money. I disagree with this view, since they can inspire people and promote understanding between nations, although careful planning is essential.

To begin with, international sporting events can inspire people and promote understanding between nations. They create national pride, encourage young people to take up sport, and bring visitors and cultural exchange. Athletes from rival countries share a stage and a set of rules, and the sight of peaceful competition can reduce prejudice. When a local athlete wins a medal, for example, thousands of children may be inspired to join clubs, which improves health for years afterwards. Events also give nations a chance to show their culture to a worldwide audience. The shared experience of watching and celebrating can unite people across social divisions.

Furthermore, events can bring economic benefits. Visitors spend money on hotels, restaurants and transport, jobs are created in construction and tourism, and new stadiums, roads and rail links may remain after the event and be used by residents. However, the costs are real. Some stadiums built for large tournaments are rarely used afterwards, leaving cities with debts, and money spent on a sporting festival might otherwise have funded schools or hospitals. For this reason, hosts should use existing venues, share events between cities and control budgets strictly. When planned carefully, international events can be a sound investment rather than a waste.

In conclusion, I disagree that international sporting events are a waste of money, because they inspire people and bring lasting benefits, provided that they are carefully planned and costs are controlled.

essays.question: To what extent do you agree or disagree that governments should ban smoking in public places?

versions.text:
Smoking harms not only the smoker but also the people around, and governments in many countries are deciding how far to restrict it. I agree that governments should ban smoking in public places, since people have a right to breathe clean air, although some flexibility may be needed outdoors.

To begin with, non-smokers have a right to breathe clean air. When smoking is allowed in enclosed places such as restaurants, offices and public transport, people who have not chosen to smoke are forced to inhale harmful smoke, which can cause asthma, heart disease and lung cancer. A waiter who works eight hours a day in a smoky restaurant, for example, breathes in harmful smoke even though he has never smoked, and he cannot easily change jobs. Children are especially at risk, since their lungs are still developing. Public places are shared by everyone, so the right to clean air should take priority over the habit of a few.

Furthermore, bans change habits and save money. They make it easier for smokers to cut down or quit, reduce litter from cigarette ends and lower the healthcare costs of smoke-related illness. Admittedly, a total ban limits personal freedom and may be difficult to enforce, particularly in open areas, and many smokers are addicted rather than careless. However, freedom to smoke does not extend to harming others, and designated outdoor areas, away from entrances and children, can balance the rights of smokers and non-smokers. Fines should be reasonable, and help for people who want to stop smoking should be widely available, so that the policy is seen as fair rather than punitive.

In conclusion, I agree that governments should ban smoking in public places, because it protects non-smokers and improves health, provided that the ban is fair and combined with support for smokers.

essays.question: Do the advantages of longer life expectancy outweigh the challenges? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Life expectancy has risen in most countries over the past century, and many people now expect to live into their eighties. This essay will discuss the main advantages and challenges before explaining whether the advantages outweigh the challenges.

On the positive side, longer lives give people more time with their families and more time to contribute. Older people pass on experience, care for grandchildren and often keep working or volunteering well beyond the traditional retirement age. A grandparent in good health, for example, can help to look after grandchildren and pass on knowledge, which supports working parents. Longer lives also reflect progress in medicine, nutrition and living conditions, and they allow people to pursue new interests, study again or start new careers later in life. Many older people today are healthy, active and valuable members of their communities.

On the negative side, ageing populations raise serious challenges. Pensions and healthcare cost more as the number of retired people grows, while there are fewer young workers to pay taxes. Illnesses such as dementia become more common, and many older people suffer from loneliness. Nevertheless, these challenges can be managed. Governments can raise the retirement age gradually, encourage saving, invest in preventive health and community care, and support older people who wish to keep working. Technology can also help older people to live independently for longer.

In conclusion, the advantages of longer life expectancy outweigh the challenges, provided that societies adapt through later retirement, better care and stronger communities.

essays.question: How can governments increase access to clean drinking water? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
Hundreds of millions of people still lack a safe supply of drinking water, and unsafe water causes serious diseases, particularly among children. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on building and maintaining infrastructure and on making water affordable, safe and well managed.

To begin with, governments should invest in water infrastructure and keep it working. Pipes, wells and treatment plants bring safe water to homes, simple filters and community-run boreholes suit remote areas, and fixing leaks and testing quality protect supplies. In many cities, a large share of water is lost through damaged pipes, so repairs can increase supply without new sources. A village that is given a protected well and a trained local committee to look after it, for example, can enjoy clean water for years, whereas an unmanaged pump soon breaks down. Planning for maintenance from the start is essential, because many projects fail when the money for repairs runs out.

In addition, authorities should make clean water affordable and protect its sources. Subsidised connections and public taps for poorer households prevent families from drinking unsafe water because they cannot pay, and clear rules with regular inspection make sure that water is tested and that polluters are punished. Equally important, education campaigns on boiling, storing and handling water, together with protection of rivers and groundwater from sewage and waste, reduce disease and keep supplies clean. International aid and partnerships with local firms can help to fund projects in poorer regions.

In conclusion, investing in reliable infrastructure and ensuring that water is affordable and protected offer the most realistic way of increasing access to clean drinking water.

crossCheck.summary: Đây là một bài khá chắc, đúng đề, bố cục gọn gàng và dùng từ chủ đề tốt, ước khoảng band 7.0. Hạn chế chính là các biện pháp được nêu khá dàn trải, ít đào sâu, và một số câu dài bị nối sai bằng dấu phẩy. Nếu phát triển ý sâu hơn và tách câu hợp lý, bài có thể lên 7.5.

Ý 'viện trợ quốc tế' không thật sự là biện pháp chính phủ trực tiếp thực hiện, làm loãng tính 'practical measures' của đề.
Nhiều câu quá dài, nối các mệnh đề độc lập chỉ bằng dấu phẩy (comma splice), ảnh hưởng độ rõ ràng.
Từ 'water' lặp lại quá nhiều lần, thiếu paraphrase đa dạng.

essays.question: Some people believe that professional athletes earn too much. Others think they deserve it. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Footballers, tennis players and basketball stars can earn more in a week than most people earn in a lifetime, and opinions differ on whether this is fair. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, those who think that professional athletes deserve their pay argue that top athletes are paid according to the revenue they create. Their careers are short, often ending before the age of forty, and injury is a constant risk. Rare talent attracts huge audiences and sponsorship, so clubs, broadcasters and advertisers earn far more than the players, and it seems reasonable that the athletes share in these profits. A player who spends fifteen years training and sacrifices a normal childhood, for example, has earned the right to be well rewarded when success comes. In a free market, pay reflects what people are willing to pay to watch.

On the other hand, critics point out that nurses and teachers, who serve society directly, earn far less. The market rewards entertainment more than public service, which many people find unfair. Enormous salaries can also distort priorities, encouraging clubs to spend huge sums on single players and pushing ticket prices out of reach of ordinary fans. Athletes are role models, and critics argue that extreme wealth may set an unhealthy example to young people about what matters in life. A nurse who saves lives every day on a modest salary, for instance, may feel undervalued next to a player paid millions to kick a ball.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that top athletes are paid fairly by market standards, but that societies should do more to reward essential jobs such as nursing and teaching.

grade.summary: Bài viết của bạn rất tốt, có bố cục chặt chẽ, luận điểm rõ ràng và đáp ứng đầy đủ yêu cầu của đề bài Discuss both views. Ngôn ngữ tự nhiên và ngữ pháp vững chắc giúp bài viết đạt mức điểm khá cao.
weaknesses: Một số cấu trúc câu còn mang tính an toàn, chưa thực sự bứt phá lên mức band 8.0+.
Ví dụ đưa ra đôi chỗ hơi dài dòng, có thể cô đọng lại để tăng tính súc tích.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết đã trả lời tốt yêu cầu đề bài, thảo luận cả hai quan điểm và đưa ra ý kiến cá nhân rõ ràng. Các luận điểm được phát triển logic và thuyết phục.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc, chia đoạn rõ ràng theo từng khía cạnh của đề bài. Các từ nối được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng nhiều cụm từ hay và chính xác trong ngữ cảnh kinh tế và xã hội. Tuy nhiên, có thể thêm một số collocation nâng cao hơn nữa để đạt band cao hơn.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức đều được kiểm soát tốt. Ngữ pháp chính xác, không có lỗi cấu trúc lớn gây cản trở người đọc.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: vận động viên chuyên nghiệp có kiếm quá nhiều không

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế gây chú ý (kiếm trong một tuần nhiều hơn người thường cả đời); mỗi thân bài một phía.

Được trả theo doanh thu tạo ra; sự nghiệp ngắn, thường kết thúc trước bốn mươi tuổi; chấn thương luôn rình rập; tài năng hiếm thu hút khán giả và nhà tài trợ nên câu lạc bộ, đài truyền hình, nhà quảng cáo kiếm nhiều hơn cầu thủ; thị trường tự do. Ví dụ cầu thủ tập mười lăm năm hy sinh tuổi thơ bình thường.

Y tá và giáo viên phục vụ xã hội trực tiếp lương thấp hơn nhiều; thị trường thưởng giải trí hơn phục vụ công; lương khổng lồ bóp méo ưu tiên, đẩy giá vé khỏi tầm với; vận động viên là hình mẫu nên giàu có cực đoan có thể truyền ý tưởng không lành mạnh. Ví dụ y tá cứu người mỗi ngày với lương khiêm tốn.
Vận động viên hàng đầu được trả hợp lý theo tiêu chuẩn thị trường nhưng xã hội nên thưởng nhiều hơn cho nghề thiết yếu.

crossCheck.summary: Đây là một bài Discuss both views chất lượng cao: trả lời đúng đề, lập trường rõ ràng, lập luận chặt chẽ và có ví dụ minh họa. Ngôn ngữ chính xác và mạch lạc, chỉ còn vài lỗi nhỏ về collocation và mạo từ. Ước tính tổng band khoảng 7.5–8.0.
weaknesses: Một số cụm chưa chuẩn về mạo từ/giới từ: 'out of reach of ordinary fans', 'an example to young people'
Câu ở thân bài 1 ('Rare talent attracts... these profits') gộp quá nhiều mệnh đề, làm giảm độ gọn gàng

essays.question: Some argue that stricter environmental laws improve public health. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Smog over cities, polluted rivers and chemicals in the soil are not only environmental issues but also health issues, and some argue that stricter environmental laws improve public health. I largely agree, although the benefits depend on enforcement and on other health measures.

To begin with, stricter environmental laws protect people from pollution-related disease. Limits on factory and vehicle emissions and on contaminated water reduce asthma, heart disease and infections, and removing lead from petrol lowered lead poisoning in children. Air pollution contributes to millions of early deaths worldwide, and cleaner air means fewer hospital admissions and longer lives. A city that bans the dirtiest vehicles from its centre, for example, may see fewer children treated for breathing problems within a few years. Safe water laws similarly prevent outbreaks of disease such as cholera, which spread quickly when drinking water is contaminated.

Furthermore, environmental laws prevent long-term harm that is hard to reverse. Controls on dangerous chemicals and waste protect farmland, rivers and food supplies, and the healthcare savings can outweigh the costs of compliance. However, the benefits are not automatic. Laws that are not enforced do little, and strict rules can raise costs for businesses and consumers, which may cause resistance. Health also depends on many other factors, such as diet, exercise, income and access to doctors, so environmental laws are only one part of the picture. They should be combined with support for industries that need to adapt.

In conclusion, stricter environmental laws improve public health to a large extent, because they reduce exposure to pollution, but their success depends on enforcement and on wider health policies.

grade.summary: Bài viết đạt chất lượng khá tốt (Band 7.0) với bố cục chặt chẽ, ngữ pháp ổn định và từ vựng liên quan đến chủ đề tốt. Tuy nhiên, việc cân đối giữa việc đồng ý và các yếu tố ngoại cảnh cần được tinh chỉnh để bài viết thuyết phục hơn ở mức điểm cao hơn.
weaknesses: Phần thân bài thứ hai đề cập khá nhiều về mặt hạn chế (enforcement, costs, other health factors) làm phân tán trọng tâm đồng ý.
Thiếu một số từ vựng mang tính học thuật cao hơn (advanced vocabulary) ở phần phát triển ý.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt câu hỏi theo hướng 'to a large extent', có đưa ra quan điểm rõ ràng và cân nhắc cả mặt hạn chế (enforcement, other factors). Tuy nhiên, lập luận về mặt hạn chế có phần lấn át phần đồng tình ở đoạn thân bài thứ hai, làm cho mức độ 'đồng ý' cần được cân bằng sắc bén hơn.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết rất tốt với các đoạn rõ ràng, câu mở đoạn và kết nối mượt mà (To begin with, Furthermore, In conclusion). Các ý tưởng được triển khai logic và có trật tự.
feedback.lexicalResource: Từ vựng khá phong phú và tự nhiên với các cụm từ liên quan đến môi trường và sức khỏe (pollution-related disease, vehicle emissions, lead poisoning). Dùng từ chính xác nhưng thiếu một vài collocation nâng cao thực sự ấn tượng.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: luật môi trường nghiêm hơn cải thiện sức khoẻ cộng đồng — largely agree

plan.think: Mở bài nối môi trường với sức khoẻ (khói bụi, sông ô nhiễm, hoá chất trong đất) rồi largely agree + giới hạn (phụ thuộc thực thi và các yếu tố khác).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — bảo vệ khỏi bệnh do ô nhiễm
plan.think: Giới hạn khí thải nhà máy, xe, nước nhiễm bẩn giảm hen, tim, nhiễm trùng; bỏ chì khỏi xăng giảm ngộ độc chì ở trẻ; ô nhiễm không khí gây hàng triệu cái chết sớm; luật nước an toàn ngăn dịch tả. Ví dụ thành phố cấm xe bẩn nhất vào trung tâm.

Có một vài chỗ diễn đạt thiếu chính xác về logic/collocation, ví dụ "limits on ... contaminated water" và "lowered lead poisoning in children".

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on birth rate initiatives or on healthcare? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
In several countries the number of births is falling while the population is ageing, and opinions differ on whether public money should go to birth rate initiatives or to healthcare. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of birth rate initiatives argue that a shrinking workforce creates serious long-term problems. With fewer young workers, there are fewer taxpayers to pay for pensions and public services, and economies may grow more slowly. Childcare support, parental leave and housing help can ease the pressure on young families who delay having children because of costs. A couple that postpones starting a family until they can afford a larger home, for example, may end up with fewer children than they wanted. If such help makes it easier to have a child, the population may stabilise over time.

On the other hand, critics point out that birth rate initiatives are expensive and their results are uncertain. People decide whether to have children for many personal reasons, and the effect of financial incentives is often small and slow. Healthcare, by contrast, benefits everyone immediately, including the growing number of older people. A healthy older population also remains active and productive for longer, which helps to offset the effects of fewer young workers. Good maternal and child health services can also help families who want children to have them safely. Investment in health therefore offers more certain returns.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that healthcare should take priority, because its benefits are immediate and certain, although modest family support can be added.

essays.question: Some argue that poor health is the main cause of social problems. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Unemployment, poverty, crime and family breakdown are often blamed on economic or political failure, but some argue that poor health is the main cause of social problems. I partly agree with this view, since illness can trigger a chain of difficulties, although it is not the only or even the main cause in every case.

To begin with, poor health can trigger a chain of social problems. Illness reduces the ability to work and earn, leads to debt and family stress, and may cause isolation or substance abuse. A father who falls ill and cannot work, for example, may plunge his family into debt and stress, and his children may miss out on education and opportunities. Mental illness that is untreated can also lead to homelessness, broken relationships and, in some cases, crime. In poorer countries, widespread disease holds back whole communities, since sick people cannot farm, study or run businesses.

However, poor health is rarely the only cause. Inequality, weak education and unemployment also create social problems independently, and they often cause poor health in the first place, so cause and effect run in both directions. A person who loses a job, for instance, may fall into poverty and then become ill because of stress, bad housing or poor diet. Social problems such as corruption, discrimination and lack of opportunity cannot be explained by health alone. Tackling them requires fair economic policies, good schools and strong institutions as well as health services. Health is therefore a major cause but part of a wider cycle.

In conclusion, poor health is an important cause of social problems, but it interacts with poverty, education and inequality, so I agree only partly that it is the main cause.

grade.summary: Bài viết có chất lượng tốt, đạt khoảng band 7.0 với lập trường rõ ràng, bố cục chặt chẽ và từ vựng phong phú. Tuy nhiên, để cải thiện lên band cao hơn, học viên cần tinh chỉnh một số cấu trúc câu và nâng cao độ chính xác của collocation.
weaknesses: Một số câu ghép dài có thể gây rối nếu đọc nhanh, cần chú ý ngắt nghỉ hoặc dùng mệnh đề quan hệ chuẩn hơn.
Vài chỗ dùng từ chưa hoàn toàn tự nhiên theo văn phong học thuật.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết trả lời tốt yêu cầu của đề bài, có lập trường rõ ràng (partly agree) ngay từ đầu và duy trì suốt bài. Các luận điểm đưa ra để ủng hộ và phản bác đều hợp lý và được phát triển đầy đủ.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với cấu trúc 4 đoạn rõ ràng. Các liên kết từ (To begin with, However, In conclusion) được sử dụng tự nhiên và hiệu quả để dẫn dắt ý.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng nhiều cụm từ hay liên quan đến chủ đề xã hội và sức khỏe (chain of difficulties, substance abuse, plunge his family into debt, cause and effect run in both directions). Tuy nhiên, một số cụm từ chưa thực sự hoàn hảo về collocation.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt giữa câu đơn và câu phức. Ngữ pháp nhìn chung chính xác, chỉ mắc một vài lỗi nhỏ về liên kết mệnh đề hoặc dấu câu.

analysis.type_vi: Extent: sức khoẻ kém là nguyên nhân chính của vấn đề xã hội — đồng ý một phần

plan.step: 1. Khung Extent với lập trường 'một phần'
plan.think: Đề nêu 'main cause' nên đồng ý một phần là hợp lý: sức khoẻ kém là nguyên nhân quan trọng nhưng không phải duy nhất hay chính trong mọi trường hợp.

Bệnh làm giảm khả năng làm việc và kiếm tiền, dẫn đến nợ và căng thẳng gia đình, cô lập hay lạm dụng chất; bệnh tâm thần không điều trị dẫn đến vô gia cư, đổ vỡ quan hệ, đôi khi phạm tội; nước nghèo bệnh tật kìm hãm cả cộng đồng. Ví dụ người cha ốm không làm việc được đẩy gia đình vào nợ.

Bất bình đẳng, giáo dục yếu, thất nghiệp tự gây vấn đề xã hội và thường gây sức khoẻ kém từ đầu: nhân quả hai chiều. Ví dụ mất việc rồi nghèo rồi ốm vì căng thẳng, nhà ở tệ. Tham nhũng, phân biệt đối xử không giải thích bằng sức khoẻ; cần chính sách kinh tế công bằng, trường tốt, thể chế mạnh.
Sức khoẻ là nguyên nhân quan trọng nhưng tương tác với nghèo, giáo dục, bất bình đẳng; đồng ý một phần.

crossCheck.summary: Đây là một bài khá tốt, vượt mốc 250 từ (285 từ), lập trường rõ ràng, lập luận hai chiều và dùng từ – ngữ pháp ở mức khá cao. Điểm hạn chế chính nằm ở việc chưa làm nổi bật 'mức độ đồng ý' như đề yêu cầu và một số cách diễn đạt còn chung chung, lặp từ. Ước lượng tổng thể: khoảng 7.5.
weaknesses: Chưa cụ thể hóa 'mức độ' đồng ý (extent) — chỉ dừng ở mức 'đồng ý một phần' chung chung mà không nói rõ mạnh hay nhẹ.
Đoạn thân 2 gom quá nhiều ý (bất bình đẳng, giáo dục, thất nghiệp, tham nhũng, phân biệt đối xử, chính sách kinh tế), khiến mỗi ý bị khai thác hời hợt.
Từ vựng đôi chỗ mơ hồ và lặp: 'difficulties', 'opportunities', 'social problems' xuất hiện nhiều lần.
Có vài chỗ diễn đạt chưa gọn và đại từ quy chiếu chưa rõ ('Tackling them...').

essays.question: In your opinion, should countries invest more in health? Explain why.

versions.text:
Ageing populations, rising costs and the lessons of recent epidemics have made health a central political issue. I firmly believe that countries should invest more in health, since healthier people are more productive and cost less in the long run, and since good health is a basic need that everyone shares.

To begin with, healthier people are more productive and cost less in the long run. A healthy workforce takes fewer sick days, works more efficiently and supports economic growth, while people who are ill or caring for sick relatives often cannot work at all. Prevention and early treatment are also much cheaper than late, emergency care. A country that funds screening and primary care, for example, may avoid expensive hospital admissions that could have been prevented. Health spending is therefore an investment that repays itself over time, rather than a pure cost.

Furthermore, strong health services make a country safer and fairer. Good hospitals, trained staff and reliable supplies allow a country to respond quickly to epidemics, which protects both lives and the economy. Access to care also gives poorer people a fair chance in life, since illness is a major cause of poverty. Admittedly, spending more on health requires higher taxes or cuts elsewhere, and money must be used efficiently to avoid waste. However, the benefits in lives saved, reduced suffering and economic strength far outweigh these costs, particularly as populations grow older.

In conclusion, I believe that countries should invest more in health, because it raises productivity, saves money in the long term and protects the most vulnerable.

grade.summary: Đây là một bài viết rất tốt, có tư duy logic rõ ràng, cấu trúc bài chuẩn IELTS và vốn từ vựng phong phú về chủ đề y tế. Bài viết hoàn thành xuất sắc yêu cầu của một bài luận Opinion.
weaknesses: Phần mở bài hơi ngắn gọn, có thể phát triển thêm một câu dẫn dắt rộng hơn.

feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác nhiều cụm từ học thuật và collocations liên quan đến chủ đề y tế (e.g., ageing populations, preventative care, primary care, emergency care). Chính tả hoàn hảo.

analysis.type_vi: Opinion: có nên đầu tư nhiều hơn vào y tế — firmly agree

plan.think: Mở bài nêu bối cảnh (già hoá, chi phí tăng, bài học dịch bệnh) rồi lập trường + hai lý do (năng suất và chi phí dài hạn; an toàn và công bằng).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — năng suất, chi phí dài hạn
plan.think: Lực lượng lao động khoẻ ít nghỉ ốm; phòng bệnh và điều trị sớm rẻ hơn cấp cứu muộn. Ví dụ nước tài trợ sàng lọc và chăm sóc ban đầu tránh nhập viện đắt.

plan.think: Bệnh viện tốt, nhân viên được đào tạo ứng phó nhanh với dịch bệnh; tiếp cận chăm sóc cho người nghèo cơ hội công bằng vì bệnh là nguyên nhân gây nghèo. Nhượng bộ: cần thuế cao hơn hoặc cắt giảm chỗ khác; phải dùng hiệu quả.

essays.question: Do the advantages of weight-loss interventions outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Obesity has become a serious health problem in many countries, and interventions to help people lose weight, from surgery and drugs to structured programmes, are increasingly common. This essay will discuss the advantages and disadvantages before explaining whether the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

On the positive side, weight-loss interventions can greatly reduce the risk of serious disease. Losing weight lowers the risk of diabetes, heart disease and joint problems and improves mobility, while surgery, drugs and structured programmes help people who have failed with dieting alone. A patient with severe obesity who has stomach surgery, for example, may lose enough weight to control diabetes and walk without pain. Improved health also brings psychological benefits, as people often feel more confident and energetic, and healthcare costs fall over time. For some patients, these treatments are the only realistic path to a healthier life.

On the negative side, however, there are real risks and costs. Surgery carries the danger of complications and requires permanent changes to eating habits, and drugs may have side effects and be very expensive. Many people regain weight after stopping a programme, and an excessive focus on appearance can lead to unhealthy attitudes to food and even eating disorders. Nevertheless, these problems can be reduced if interventions are supervised by qualified professionals, offered to those with a genuine medical need and combined with advice on diet, exercise and mental health.

In conclusion, the advantages of weight-loss interventions outweigh the disadvantages for people at serious medical risk, provided that treatment is carefully supervised and supported over the long term.

Thiếu các từ vựng và cấu trúc câu ở mức độ nâng cao (band 8+).

analysis.type_vi: A/D: can thiệp giảm cân — lợi thế có lớn hơn bất lợi không (advantages outweigh cho người có nguy cơ y tế)

plan.think: Phán quyết có điều kiện (người có nguy cơ y tế nghiêm trọng); thân bài 2 dùng Nevertheless để phản bác.

Giảm nguy cơ tiểu đường, tim, khớp; cải thiện vận động; phẫu thuật, thuốc, chương trình giúp người không giảm được bằng ăn kiêng; lợi ích tâm lý; chi phí y tế giảm. Ví dụ bệnh nhân béo phì nặng mổ dạ dày kiểm soát được tiểu đường.

Phẫu thuật có biến chứng, đòi hỏi thay đổi ăn uống vĩnh viễn; thuốc có tác dụng phụ, đắt; nhiều người tăng cân lại; quá tập trung vào ngoại hình gây rối loạn ăn uống. Nevertheless: giám sát bởi chuyên gia, chỉ cho người có nhu cầu y tế thật, kèm tư vấn.
Lợi thế lớn hơn cho người có nguy cơ nghiêm trọng nếu được giám sát và hỗ trợ lâu dài.

essays.question: How far do you think animal testing will change in the next 20 years? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Animal testing has long been a controversial part of medical and product research, and I believe that it will change considerably over the next twenty years, becoming less common as alternatives improve, although it will probably not disappear completely.

First and foremost, new technology is providing alternatives to animal experiments. Scientists can now grow tiny organs from human cells, use computer models to predict how drugs behave in the body and test substances on chips that copy the function of organs. These methods are often cheaper and faster, and they use human cells, which may predict human reactions better than animals do. A cosmetic company that tests safety on lab-grown skin, for example, no longer needs to use rabbits. As artificial intelligence improves, such predictions will become even more reliable.

In addition, rules and public opinion are moving in the same direction. Many governments already ban animal testing for cosmetics, and research bodies follow the principle of replacing animals where possible, using fewer of them and treating them humanely. Companies know that customers increasingly dislike animal experiments, which gives them a reason to switch. However, change will have limits. A whole living body is far more complex than any model, and regulators may continue to require animal studies for the safety of new medicines until alternatives are proven. Progress will therefore be steady rather than sudden.

In conclusion, animal testing is likely to change to a large extent over the next twenty years because of better technology and stronger rules, although some use for complex medical research will probably remain.

essays.question: What are the causes of teen substance abuse? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
Alcohol, tobacco and illegal drugs are used by a worrying number of teenagers, and the habit can damage their health and education for years. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Teenagers turn to drugs and alcohol because of peer pressure, stress and easy access. Friends who use substances make it seem normal, family problems and school pressure create a wish to escape, and curiosity combined with a lack of knowledge about the risks leads some young people to experiment. A fifteen-year-old at a party where everyone is drinking, for example, may accept a drink simply to avoid being left out. In addition, substances are often cheap and easy to obtain, and advertising, films and social media can make them look glamorous. Teenage brains are still developing, which makes young people more impulsive and more vulnerable to addiction. Early use can then develop into dependence and damage health, relationships and exam results.

To address this issue, prevention should combine education, support and strict control of sales. Schools can explain the real risks, and sessions led by former users can be more convincing than warnings from adults. Counselling helps teenagers with stress and family difficulties, and enforcement stops shops from selling to minors. Clubs, sport and youth centres give young people healthy alternatives and a sense of belonging. In addition, treatment services must be available for those who already have a problem, and parents need advice on how to talk to their children without anger. Prevention is far less costly than dealing with addiction later, and it protects the futures of young people.

In conclusion, teenage substance abuse stems mainly from peer pressure, stress and easy access, but education, family support and firm enforcement offer a realistic way forward.

essays.question: How can governments support mental health in the workplace? Suggest practical measures.

versions.text:
Stress, depression and burnout are among the leading reasons for absence from work, and many employees are afraid to admit that they are struggling. This essay will suggest practical measures that governments could take, focusing on laws and standards for employers and on services and awareness.

To begin with, governments should require and encourage mentally healthy workplaces. Laws on working hours and workload, free counselling, training for managers, flexible hours and campaigns against stigma help employees to cope before stress becomes illness. An employee who is expected to answer emails late at night, for example, may develop anxiety long before anyone notices, so limits on out-of-hours contact can protect wellbeing. Employers could be required to assess psychological risks, just as they must assess physical hazards, and tax benefits or public recognition could reward companies that do this well. Small firms need advice and templates, since they rarely have specialist staff.

In addition, authorities should provide accessible services and promote awareness. Affordable counselling and helplines, available outside working hours, give employees somewhere to turn, and mental health first-aid training enables colleagues to recognise warning signs. Public campaigns that present mental illness as a health condition, not a weakness, make workers more willing to ask for help early. Equally important, support for people returning to work after illness, such as gradual return plans, prevents relapse. Such measures cost less than the loss of productivity and the sick pay that result from untreated problems, and they help to retain experienced staff.

In conclusion, setting clear workplace standards and providing accessible services and awareness campaigns offer the most realistic way of supporting mental health in the workplace.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on child nutrition programs? Use examples.

versions.text:
Hunger and poor nutrition still hold back millions of children, even in countries that are not poor. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on child nutrition programmes: healthier, better-performing children, and long-term savings and opportunity.

First and foremost, child nutrition programmes help children to grow, learn and stay healthy. Well-fed children concentrate better, attend school more regularly and suffer fewer illnesses, so they are more likely to finish their education. A child who receives a free school breakfast, for example, is less likely to feel tired and distracted in morning lessons. Programmes that provide meals, milk, fruit or vitamins also reduce stunting and anaemia, which can harm a child's development for life. Teachers report that children who eat properly behave better, and parents on low incomes are relieved of a daily worry.

In addition, nutrition programmes bring long-term savings and opportunity. Healthier children grow into healthier adults who work more productively and need less medical care, so the cost of the programme is repaid many times over. Because poor children benefit most, the programmes help to break the cycle of poverty, since education and health are the main routes out of it. They can also support local farmers if schools buy fresh produce from nearby farms, and they teach children about food and cooking. Although providing meals requires organisation and money, careful targeting and local sourcing can keep costs under control. Countries such as Brazil and India have run large school meal schemes, which suggests that this approach is practical.

To sum up, child nutrition programmes bring clear benefits to a country, above all healthier, better-educated children and long-term savings. For these reasons, they deserve sustained public support.

essays.question: Many people say that a healthy diet prevents illness. Do you agree or disagree? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Doctors and health campaigns constantly advise people to eat well, and many people say that a healthy diet prevents illness. I largely agree with this view, since good food lowers the risk of many serious diseases, although a healthy diet cannot guarantee good health on its own.

To begin with, a healthy diet lowers the risk of many serious illnesses. Eating plenty of vegetables, fruit and whole grains and little processed food reduces the chance of heart disease, type 2 diabetes and some cancers. Such foods supply vitamins, fibre and minerals that keep the body working properly, while diets high in salt, sugar and fat are linked to high blood pressure and obesity. A person who replaces fried snacks and fizzy drinks with fruit, nuts and water, for example, may lower their blood pressure within months and reduce the chance of needing medication later. Good nutrition also strengthens the immune system, so the body fights infections more effectively.

Furthermore, the effect on children can last a lifetime. Children who learn to enjoy balanced meals are likely to carry those habits into adulthood and to avoid weight problems. However, diet is only one factor. Genes, infections, accidents, air pollution and stress also affect health, so a person can eat well and still become ill. Exercise, sleep, avoiding smoking and regular medical checks are equally important. Diet should therefore be seen as an important part of prevention, not a guarantee. People should not blame themselves too harshly when illness occurs despite careful eating.

In conclusion, I largely agree that a healthy diet prevents illness, because it reduces the risk of major diseases, although it works best alongside other healthy habits and cannot remove every risk.

essays.question: What are the causes of limited access to healthcare in rural areas? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
People in rural areas often live far from hospitals and doctors, and their health is generally worse than that of city dwellers. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Rural areas struggle to attract doctors and keep clinics open. Medical staff often prefer cities for higher pay, better schools for their children and more career opportunities, while patients in the countryside face long journeys, poor roads and low incomes. A villager with chest pain, for example, may have to travel two hours to the nearest hospital, and many do not go at all. In addition, rural populations tend to be older and poorer, so their need is greater, while the number of patients in each village is too small to make a clinic profitable. As a result, people delay seeking help, and illnesses are found late, when treatment is harder and more costly.

To address this issue, governments should bring doctors and services closer to rural communities. Higher pay, housing and loan forgiveness attract staff, and training local students encourages them to return to serve their own area. Mobile clinics, telemedicine and community health workers reach remote villages at a lower cost, so that minor problems can be treated nearby and only serious cases need to travel. Improving roads and providing emergency transport would also shorten journeys when hospital care is needed. These measures are expensive, but they cost less than treating advanced disease and the loss of working lives that follows.

In conclusion, limited access to healthcare in rural areas stems mainly from shortages of staff and long distances, but incentives, local training and mobile services offer a realistic way forward.

essays.question: What are the benefits for a country that focuses on early disease detection programs? Use examples.

versions.text:
Many serious diseases are easier to treat if they are found early, and some countries run programmes to test large numbers of people before symptoms appear. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on early disease detection programmes: better survival and health, and savings for the health system and economy.

First and foremost, detecting disease early makes treatment simpler, cheaper and more successful. Screening for cancer, diabetes and heart disease finds problems before symptoms appear, when a small operation or medicine may be enough, whereas late discovery needs long and costly care. A woman whose breast cancer is found at a routine scan, for example, may need only a small operation and be back at work within weeks. As a result, more people survive, suffer less and keep their independence. Children can also be checked for hearing and vision problems, so that they receive help before they fall behind at school.

In addition, early detection brings savings and economic benefits. Treating advanced disease requires long hospital stays, expensive drugs and sometimes lifelong care, while early treatment costs much less. Healthy workers remain productive, and families are spared the loss of income and the emotional strain of serious illness. Although screening programmes require equipment, trained staff and public awareness, and sometimes produce false alarms, these costs are small compared with the benefits. Wider use of simple tests, such as blood pressure checks, can also be extended to rural areas through mobile services, so that everyone benefits and inequalities in health are reduced.

To sum up, early disease detection programmes bring clear benefits to a country, above all better survival and lower costs. For these reasons, they deserve sustained public support.

essays.question: Some people believe that healthy eating should be promoted through taxation on unhealthy foods. Others disagree. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Obesity and diet-related disease are rising in many countries, and some people believe that healthy eating should be promoted through taxation on unhealthy foods. Others disagree. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of such a tax argue that it sends a clear price signal. Higher prices reduce consumption of sugary drinks and snacks, encourage manufacturers to reduce sugar and fat in their recipes, and raise revenue that can be spent on health services. Some countries that taxed sugary drinks saw sales fall and recipes change, which suggests that the policy can work. Taxes are also cheaper to run than many other measures, since they use the existing tax system. A tax on soft drinks, for example, can persuade a company to cut the sugar in its best-selling product rather than pay more. If the money is used to subsidise fruit and vegetables or to fund school meals, the benefit is greater still.

On the other hand, critics point out that taxes on food hit poorer households hardest. People on low incomes spend a larger share of their money on food, and they may simply switch to another cheap unhealthy product, so the higher price alone does not improve their diet. Taxes may also seem unfair, as they punish people instead of helping them. Education, better access to fresh food and clear labels may achieve more in the long run. A family that lives far from a market selling fresh vegetables, for instance, will not eat better just because chips cost more.

To sum up, both positions have their merits; nevertheless, I believe that a tax can be useful if its revenue is used to make healthy food cheaper and more accessible, rather than as a punishment alone.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on public health campaigns or on hospital infrastructure? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether public money should be spent mainly on public health campaigns or on hospital infrastructure. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of public health campaigns argue that preventing illness is cheaper and kinder than treating it. Campaigns against smoking, poor diet and infectious disease reach millions of people at a relatively low cost and can change habits that cause serious illness. Vaccination drives and health education stop disease before it starts, so fewer people ever need a hospital bed. A campaign that teaches handwashing, for example, can reduce infections in schools at very little cost. Over time, a healthier population also means lower spending on treatment and more people able to work.

On the other hand, advocates of hospital infrastructure point out that people who are already ill need treatment now. Campaigns cannot cure disease, accidents and genetic conditions cannot be prevented, and hospitals need modern buildings, equipment and staff to cope with emergencies and an ageing population. A rural hospital without a scanner, for instance, must send patients on long journeys that can delay diagnosis. Old, overcrowded facilities also put staff under pressure and increase waiting times. A health system that neglects treatment loses public trust, however good its campaigns may be.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that prevention deserves a growing share of the budget because it offers the best long-term value, while hospitals must still receive enough money to provide safe, modern care for those who need it today.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether public money should be spent mainly on public health campaigns or on hospital infrastructure. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of public health campaigns argue that preventing illness is cheaper and kinder than treating it. Campaigns against smoking, poor diet and infectious disease reach millions of people at a relatively low cost and can change habits that cause serious illness. Vaccination drives and health education stop disease before it starts, so fewer people ever need a hospital bed. A campaign that teaches handwashing, for example, can reduce infections in schools at very little cost. Over time, a healthier population also means lower spending on treatment and more people able to work. Campaigns can also be adjusted quickly when new health threats appear.

On the other hand, advocates of hospital infrastructure point out that people who are already ill need treatment now. Campaigns cannot cure disease, accidents and genetic conditions cannot be prevented, and hospitals need modern buildings, equipment and staff to cope with emergencies and an ageing population. A rural hospital without a scanner, for instance, must send patients on long journeys that can delay diagnosis. Old, overcrowded facilities also put staff under pressure and increase waiting times. A health system that neglects treatment loses public trust, however good its campaigns may be.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that prevention deserves a growing share of the budget because it offers the best long-term value, while hospitals must still receive enough money to provide safe, modern care for those who need it today.

essays.question: Some people prefer traditional medicine while others prefer modern medicine. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Many people turn to herbal remedies, acupuncture and other traditional methods, while others rely entirely on hospitals and modern drugs. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of traditional medicine value its gentle, holistic approach and cultural roots. Remedies such as herbal teas and massage have been used for centuries, are often cheaper and may cause fewer obvious side effects, and practitioners usually spend time listening to patients and considering their whole lifestyle. For many communities, traditional practices are familiar and trusted, and some, such as acupuncture for certain kinds of pain, have been supported by research. A person with mild stomach trouble, for example, may find relief from a simple herbal tea and prefer it to a strong tablet. Traditional medicine can also be an important part of cultural identity.

On the other hand, supporters of modern medicine point out that it is tested and proven. Treatments such as vaccines, antibiotics and surgery have been checked in trials and save millions of lives, whereas many herbal remedies have not been properly studied and may be ineffective or harmful in the wrong dose. A person with a serious infection, for instance, may become dangerously ill if they rely only on herbs and delay proper treatment. Modern medicine can be expensive and sometimes impersonal, but its evidence base is far stronger, and it can deal with emergencies and serious conditions.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that modern medicine should be the main choice for serious illness, while traditional methods can be used alongside it for comfort and minor complaints, provided that they are safe.

essays.question: Discuss the role of youth sports programs in physical and social development.

versions.text:
Football clubs, swimming squads and school teams give millions of young people the chance to play, and their value goes beyond winning matches. This essay will outline two key roles that youth sports programmes play in young people's development: building physical fitness and health, and developing social and personal skills.

First and foremost, youth sports programmes build fitness and good habits. Regular training develops strength, coordination and stamina, and children who enjoy sport are more likely to stay active for life, which lowers the risk of obesity, diabetes and heart disease. Sport also offers a healthy way to use energy and improves sleep and concentration, which helps pupils at school. A child who struggles to sit still in class, for example, may benefit from a daily run around a playing field. As children spend more time on screens, organised sport offers an important counterbalance.

In addition, youth sports programmes develop social and personal skills. Team play teaches cooperation, discipline and how to cope with winning and losing, and clubs give young people friends and positive role models. A shy teenager who joins a basketball team, for example, often gains confidence and makes friends. Coaches and teammates can also give support to those who face difficulties at home, and young people who are busy with training have less time to get into trouble. However, programmes must be managed carefully. Excessive pressure to win, injuries, high costs and the exclusion of weaker players can discourage children, so clubs should welcome all abilities and emphasise enjoyment and fair play.

To sum up, youth sports programmes play a valuable role in physical and social development by building fitness and by teaching teamwork and confidence. For these reasons, they deserve continued support.

essays.question: Should individuals be responsible for their own healthcare costs, or should society/government fund care? Discuss.

versions.text:
The cost of modern medicine is rising, and people disagree about who should pay for it: individuals themselves, or society through the government. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of individual payment argue that people should take responsibility for the cost of their own care. When patients pay something, even a small fee, they tend to use services more carefully, which reduces waste and unnecessary visits. Individual payment can also keep taxes lower and allows people to choose the level of cover that suits them. Competition between private providers may improve quality and shorten waiting times, since clinics must attract patients. A small charge for a routine consultation, for example, may discourage people from seeing a doctor for minor complaints that could be treated at home, leaving more time for those who are seriously ill.

On the other hand, advocates of public funding point out that illness is unpredictable and expensive, so the cost of care should be shared. A serious illness can ruin a family's finances through no fault of its own, and people who delay treatment because they cannot pay often need costlier emergency care later. Public funding protects the poor, keeps the workforce healthy and treats health as a basic right rather than a luxury. A patient who cannot afford cancer treatment, for instance, may lose both health and savings. Shared funding spreads the risk across the whole population, so that no one is left without help.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that society should fund essential care, with modest personal contributions for non-urgent services, because this protects the vulnerable while limiting waste.

essays.question: Discuss how public campaigns can change health behaviours.

versions.text:
Advertisements for soap, soft drinks and cars change what people buy, and governments hope that public health campaigns can change behaviour in the same way. This essay will explain two key ways in which public campaigns change health behaviours: by spreading simple messages widely and by changing what people see as normal.

First and foremost, public health campaigns reach millions of people at a low cost per person. Television, social media, schools and posters can spread simple, repeated messages about smoking, handwashing, vaccination or diet, and well-known figures and real stories make the advice memorable. A campaign that shows the real story of a former smoker, for example, can persuade more people to quit than a list of statistics. Messages that give a clear, easy action, such as washing hands for twenty seconds, are more likely to be remembered and followed than general warnings.

In addition, campaigns change social attitudes. When wearing a seat belt or avoiding smoking in public is shown as normal and responsible, people tend to follow the example of those around them, and young people learn what is expected. However, information alone does not change behaviour if people cannot act on it. People may know that vegetables are healthy but lack the money or time to buy them, and messages that lecture or frighten can be ignored. Campaigns therefore work best when combined with services, rules and prices that support the advice, such as free vaccination, taxes on tobacco or healthier school meals. Evaluating results and adjusting the message also improves success.

To sum up, public campaigns can change health behaviours by spreading memorable messages and shaping social norms, but they are most effective when supported by practical measures. For these reasons, they should be one part of a wider strategy.

essays.question: Do the advantages of shorter hospital stays outweigh the risks? Give reasons and examples.

versions.text:
Hospital stays have become much shorter in many countries, with some patients going home on the day of an operation. This essay will discuss the advantages and the risks before explaining whether the advantages outweigh them.

On the positive side, shorter hospital stays lower costs and free beds for other patients. Modern techniques such as keyhole surgery and better pain relief allow earlier recovery, and patients at home avoid hospital infections and recover in comfort, surrounded by family. A patient who has a hip replacement and walks home within two days, for example, frees a bed for someone else on the waiting list. Hospitals can therefore treat more people with the same resources, and waiting lists become shorter. Many patients also report that they sleep better and feel less anxious in their own homes.

On the negative side, patients sent home too early may suffer complications. Problems can go unnoticed without nurses nearby, older people who live alone may lack help, and family members often have to act as unpaid carers. Some patients return to hospital, which cancels out the savings. Nevertheless, these risks can be managed. Hospitals can use clear criteria to decide who is safe to leave, arrange follow-up phone calls and home visits by nurses, and provide remote monitoring for those at greater risk. Good information for patients and families, with a number to call if something seems wrong, also gives reassurance.

In conclusion, the advantages of shorter hospital stays outweigh the risks, provided that patients are carefully selected and given proper support at home.

essays.question: What are the causes of poor sanitation in urban slums? What solutions can be proposed?

versions.text:
In many fast-growing cities, millions of people live in crowded slums where toilets, drains and rubbish collection are inadequate, and diseases such as cholera and diarrhoea spread easily. This essay will analyse the principal causes and propose realistic solutions.

Rapid migration into cities outpaces the building of basic services. People who cannot afford housing settle in informal areas outside official planning, where there are no sewers, toilets or rubbish collection, and weak local governments lack the money or authority to provide them. In a settlement where hundreds of people share a few toilets, for example, waste can easily reach drinking water. In addition, residents without legal rights to their land fear eviction, so neither they nor the authorities invest in permanent improvements. High housing costs and low incomes keep people in these conditions for years, and children suffer most from the resulting illnesses.

To address this issue, upgrading existing settlements is faster and fairer than clearing them. Toilets, drains and rubbish collection can be added step by step, legal recognition gives residents a reason to invest in their own homes, and community participation keeps facilities clean and maintained. Governments should also build affordable housing and extend water and sewerage networks as cities grow, so that new arrivals are not forced into informal areas. Hygiene education, for instance on handwashing and safe waste disposal, helps families to protect their health at little cost. Health improves without forcing families to move, and the economy benefits from healthier workers.

In conclusion, poor sanitation in urban slums stems mainly from rapid migration and a lack of planning and secure land rights, but upgrading, legal recognition and community involvement offer a realistic way forward.

essays.question: Is it better to focus government spending on preventive healthcare or on treatment services? Discuss and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Opinions are divided as to whether public money should be spent mainly on preventive healthcare or on treatment services. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of prevention argue that stopping illness before it develops is cheaper and kinder than curing it. Regular screening, vaccination and advice on diet, exercise and smoking identify problems early, when they are simple and inexpensive to deal with. A cancer found at an early stage, for example, may be treated with minor surgery, whereas the same disease found late may require years of costly care. Preventive measures also keep people productive and independent, and each unit of money spent on prevention can save several times as much on treatment later. Healthy habits learned in childhood can last a lifetime.

On the other hand, supporters of treatment services point out that illness cannot always be prevented. Accidents, genetic conditions and infections strike even careful people, and those who are already sick need skilled help immediately, not advice about their future. Hospitals, emergency teams and specialist doctors save lives every day, and the public rightly expects the state to provide them. A patient with a broken spine, for instance, depends on emergency treatment and long-term rehabilitation, not on prevention campaigns. Reducing treatment budgets would cause suffering and anger.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that prevention should receive a larger share than it does now because it offers better long-term value, but treatment must remain well funded so that nobody is left without care.

essays.question: Discuss the role of arts therapy in mental health treatment.

versions.text:
Painting, music, drama and dance are usually seen as leisure activities, but they are increasingly used by trained therapists to help people with mental health problems. This essay will outline two roles that arts therapy plays in treatment: giving patients a means of expression and supporting wellbeing alongside other treatments.

First and foremost, arts therapy gives people a way to express feelings that they cannot put into words. Painting, music and drama allow patients to explore painful experiences safely, reduce stress and build confidence, which helps those who find talking therapy difficult. A child who cannot speak about a frightening experience, for example, may be able to show it through drawing, and the therapist can then help the child to talk about it. People with dementia or autism, and survivors of trauma, may also respond to music or art when words fail. Creating something can give a sense of control and achievement to those who feel helpless.

In addition, arts therapy supports wellbeing alongside other treatments. Group sessions reduce loneliness by bringing people together, and the focus on creating something shifts attention away from worries and symptoms. Many hospitals now include art or music sessions in their care for conditions such as depression, anxiety and addiction. However, arts therapy is not a replacement for medication or counselling in serious illness, and evidence of its benefits, though encouraging, is still developing. It works best alongside, not instead of, other treatments, and it requires trained professionals so that patients are protected.

To sum up, arts therapy plays a valuable role in mental health treatment by offering a gentle way to express feelings and by supporting recovery. For these reasons, it deserves continued support.

essays.question: How far do you think wearable health tech will change patient monitoring in the next 20 years? Support your answer with reasons.

versions.text:
Watches that count heartbeats and patches that measure blood sugar are becoming common, and I believe that wearable health technology will change patient monitoring considerably over the next twenty years, although it will not replace regular medical care.

First and foremost, wearable devices allow continuous monitoring outside hospital. Watches and patches record heart rate, blood sugar and sleep all day, warn of problems early and let patients with long-term illness manage their condition at home. A watch that detects an irregular heartbeat, for example, may prompt its wearer to see a doctor before a stroke occurs. Instead of a single reading in a clinic every few months, doctors will see trends over weeks, which gives a far more accurate picture of a patient's health. Hospitals could then send patients home earlier, with their condition watched remotely.

In addition, wearables will become smaller, cheaper and more powerful. Artificial intelligence will analyse the data and alert doctors only when something changes, so that patients get help in time and doctors are not overwhelmed. This approach is especially valuable for older people and those with heart disease or diabetes. However, there are limits. Some devices are not accurate enough for medical decisions, large amounts of data may overload doctors, and privacy and security of personal information are serious concerns. Older or poorer patients may also find the technology difficult or too costly to use.

In conclusion, wearable health technology is likely to change patient monitoring to a large extent by enabling continuous, remote and early detection, provided that accuracy, privacy and fair access are ensured.

essays.question: Some argue that stricter food safety regulations protect public health. To what extent do you agree?

versions.text:
Contaminated food can make large numbers of people ill within a few hours, and some argue that stricter food safety regulations protect public health. I largely agree, since strong rules prevent outbreaks and build trust, although they must be fair and enforceable.

To begin with, strict food safety rules protect public health. Inspections, hygiene standards and traceability reduce outbreaks of food poisoning and allow contaminated products to be recalled quickly, which builds trust in the food industry. A restaurant that stores raw meat next to salad, for example, can cause an outbreak of food poisoning that affects dozens of customers. Rules about cooking temperatures, cleaning, storage and labelling of allergens remove many of these risks. Because consumers cannot see bacteria or check a factory for themselves, they depend on regulation to keep food safe, and children, older people and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable.

Furthermore, regulations create a level playing field and support trade. Honest producers are not undercut by careless ones who save money by ignoring hygiene, and exporters need to meet high standards to sell in other countries. After a serious scandal, the damage to an entire industry can be far greater than the cost of prevention. However, strict rules also have costs. Small farmers and local sellers may find paperwork and equipment expensive, and enforcement requires well-trained inspectors. Authorities should therefore apply proportionate rules, give advice and time to small businesses, and focus inspections on the highest risks, so that safety is improved without destroying livelihoods.

In conclusion, stricter food safety regulations protect public health to a large extent, because they prevent illness and build trust, provided that they are proportionate and well enforced.

essays.question: Many people think that DIY healthcare information online is risky. Do you agree? Explain with examples.

versions.text:
Millions of people now type their symptoms into a search engine before they ever see a doctor, and many feel that do-it-yourself healthcare information online is risky. I largely agree, although such information can also be useful when used with care.

To begin with, medical advice found online can be unreliable and risky. Websites and social media mix expert advice with rumour and advertising, and people who diagnose themselves may panic over minor symptoms or ignore serious ones. A person who searches online for the cause of a headache, for example, may be convinced that it is something deadly when it is only stress, while another may dismiss a warning sign because a forum said it was harmless. Some sites also sell unproven remedies, and following false advice can delay proper treatment or cause harm directly.

Furthermore, online information cannot replace an examination by a trained professional. A doctor can ask follow-up questions, check the body and arrange tests, whereas a website gives general information that may not apply to the individual. People may also take medicines in the wrong dose or combine them dangerously. However, online information is not always harmful. Reputable health services and hospitals publish clear, accurate guidance, and well-informed patients can ask better questions and understand their treatment. The key is to use trusted sources and to check anything serious with a professional.

In conclusion, I largely agree that do-it-yourself healthcare information online is risky, because it can mislead and delay treatment, although it is valuable when it comes from reliable sources and is used as a first step, not a final answer.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết đã trả lời rõ ràng câu hỏi theo hướng đồng ý một phần (largely agree) và đưa ra các lập luận cũng như ví dụ cụ thể. Tuy nhiên, việc đưa phần phản biện (online information is not always harmful) vào giữa thân bài thứ hai làm cấu trúc lập luận hơi bị phân tán thay vì tách hẳn một đoạn phản biện riêng.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Các đoạn văn được liên kết khá tốt bằng các từ nối như 'To begin with', 'Furthermore', 'However', 'In conclusion'. Bố cục mạch lạc, người đọc dễ theo dõi mạch suy nghĩ của tác giả từ đầu đến cuối.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng linh hoạt các cụm từ chủ đề y tế và công nghệ như 'search engine', 'do-it-yourself healthcare', 'unproven remedies', 'reputable health services'. Tuy nhiên, một số cụm từ có thể được nâng cấp để đạt độ tự nhiên và học thuật cao hơn ở mức band cao.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, kết hợp tốt giữa câu đơn và câu phức với các mệnh đề trạng ngữ. Ngữ pháp chính xác, không có lỗi cấu trúc lớn gây cản trở việc đọc hiểu.

analysis.type_vi: Agree/Disagree: thông tin y tế tự tìm trên mạng có rủi ro — largely agree

plan.think: Mở bài bằng thói quen quen thuộc (gõ triệu chứng vào công cụ tìm kiếm trước khi gặp bác sĩ) rồi largely agree + nhượng bộ (có ích nếu dùng cẩn thận).

plan.step: 2. Lý do 1 — thông tin không đáng tin
plan.think: Trang web và mạng xã hội trộn lời khuyên chuyên gia với tin đồn, quảng cáo; tự chẩn đoán gây hoảng loạn hoặc chủ quan; bán thuốc chưa chứng minh. Ví dụ tìm nguyên nhân đau đầu tưởng bệnh nặng trong khi chỉ là căng thẳng.

plan.step: 3. Lý do 2 — không thay thế khám + nhượng bộ
plan.think: Bác sĩ hỏi thêm, khám cơ thể, làm xét nghiệm; thông tin chung có thể không đúng với cá nhân; uống sai liều, kết hợp thuốc nguy hiểm. Nhượng bộ: trang uy tín của bệnh viện cung cấp hướng dẫn chính xác; người bệnh hiểu biết hỏi tốt hơn; cần nguồn đáng tin và kiểm tra với chuyên gia.
Rủi ro nhưng có giá trị nếu từ nguồn đáng tin và là bước đầu chứ không phải câu trả lời cuối cùng.

essays.question: Some people prefer animal testing while others prefer alternatives. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

versions.text:
Some scientists still rely on experiments with animals to test new drugs, while others prefer alternatives such as cell cultures and computer models. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of animal testing argue that it gives results that other methods cannot yet match. A living animal has blood circulation, an immune system and organs that interact, so researchers can see how a drug is absorbed, spread and removed from the whole body, and whether it harms any organ. This is essential for safety, because a medicine that seems harmless in a dish may damage the liver or heart in a living creature. A new painkiller, for example, may look safe in cells but cause serious side effects in a whole body. Regulators in many countries still ask for animal data before trials in people.

On the other hand, supporters of alternatives point out that these methods can be faster, cheaper and more relevant to people. Human cells, lab-grown organs and computer simulations can predict human reactions better than animals, whose biology differs from ours, and they avoid animal suffering. A drug that works safely in a mouse can fail in humans, wasting years and money, whereas tests on human tissue may give more reliable answers. Alternatives also allow thousands of substances to be screened rapidly.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that alternatives should be used wherever they are reliable, with animal testing kept only for cases where no other method can answer the safety question.

grade.summary: Bài viết có bố cục tốt, lập luận chặt chẽ và từ vựng phong phú về chủ đề thử nghiệm trên động vật. Người viết cần cải thiện thêm sự đa dạng trong cấu trúc ngữ pháp và từ vựng nâng cao để đạt band điểm cao hơn.
weaknesses: Một số ý kiến và ví dụ còn mang tính phổ thông, chưa có các thuật ngữ chuyên ngành sâu hơn.
Thiếu các cấu trúc câu phức nâng cao (như đảo ngữ hoặc mệnh đề phân từ rút gọn).
Quan điểm cá nhân ở phần kết luận có phần an toàn, có thể đào sâu hơn về mặt triết lý hoặc thực tiễn.

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết đã thảo luận cả hai quan điểm và đưa ra quan điểm cá nhân rõ ràng ở phần mở bài và kết bài. Các ý tưởng được phát triển khá tốt, đáp ứng đủ yêu cầu của đề bài.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết mạch lạc với các đoạn mở bài, thân bài và kết bài rõ ràng. Việc sử dụng các từ nối như 'On the one hand', 'On the other hand' và 'In conclusion' rất hiệu quả.
feedback.lexicalResource: Từ vựng được sử dụng tự nhiên, chính xác và phù hợp với chủ đề khoa học và y tế. Tuy nhiên, có thể bổ sung thêm các từ vựng nâng cao hơn để đạt điểm cao hơn.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc câu đa dạng, từ câu đơn đến câu phức đều được kiểm soát tốt. Ngữ pháp chính xác, không có lỗi nghiêm trọng ảnh hưởng đến việc hiểu nghĩa.

weaknesses: Một số lập luận còn hơi đơn giản, chưa khai thác hết các khía cạnh đạo đức sâu xa
Từ vựng ở mức độ an toàn, thiếu các cụm từ học thuật nâng cao (advanced collocations)

feedback.taskResponse: Bài viết đã thảo luận đầy đủ cả hai quan điểm về thử nghiệm trên động vật và các phương pháp thay thế, đồng thời đưa ra quan điểm cá nhân rõ ràng ở phần mở bài và kết bài. Các ý chính được phát triển khá tốt với các ví dụ cụ thể, mặc dù lập trường cá nhân trong kết bài có phần hơi an toàn nhưng vẫn hoàn toàn hợp lý.
feedback.coherenceCohesion: Bố cục bài viết rõ ràng với cấu trúc 4 đoạn chuẩn mực. Các từ nối và phương tiện liên kết được sử dụng mượt mà, giúp người đọc dễ dàng theo dõi dòng suy nghĩ và sự chuyển đổi giữa các quan điểm.
feedback.lexicalResource: Vốn từ vựng phong phú, sử dụng chính xác các thuật ngữ liên quan đến chủ đề khoa học và y tế như 'cell cultures', 'computer simulations', 'side effects', và 'screened rapidly'. Tuy nhiên, có thể nâng cấp thêm một số cụm từ học thuật nâng cao để đạt điểm cao hơn ở tiêu chí này.
feedback.grammar: Cấu trúc ngữ pháp đa dạng, kết hợp linh hoạt giữa câu đơn, câu ghép và câu phức với tỷ lệ mắc lỗi rất thấp. Các thì và sự hòa hợp giữa chủ ngữ và động từ được kiểm soát tốt xuyên suốt bài viết.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: thích thử nghiệm trên động vật hay phương án thay thế (góc khoa học và thực tiễn, khác 105 là đạo đức)

plan.think: Đề 493 so sánh phương pháp nên tập trung vào độ chính xác, tốc độ, chi phí thay vì đạo đức (đã dùng ở 105).

Động vật sống có tuần hoàn, hệ miễn dịch, cơ quan tương tác nên nhà nghiên cứu thấy thuốc được hấp thu, phân bố, thải ra thế thế nào và có hại cơ quan nào; thuốc vô hại trong đĩa có thể hại gan hoặc tim; cơ quan quản lý vẫn yêu cầu. Ví dụ thuốc giảm đau.
Nhanh, rẻ, liên quan hơn cho con người: tế bào người, cơ quan nuôi, mô phỏng máy tính; sinh học động vật khác người; thuốc an toàn trên chuột có thể hỏng trên người; sàng lọc hàng nghìn chất nhanh.
Dùng phương án thay thế khi đáng tin; chỉ giữ thử nghiệm động vật khi không có cách khác trả lời câu hỏi an toàn.
